hints: Focus on how bonding and acid-base character change across Period 3, from ionic basic on the left to covalent acidic on the right.
Check statement 2 first. Think about what happens when $\text{AlCl}_3$ is added to water and whether the $\text{[Al(H}_2\text{O)}_6\text{]}^{3+}$ ion stays neutral.
Link electronegativity to bonding type. Identify the two elements furthest right and decide what type of chloride they must form.
walkthrough:
**Sort the Period 3 oxides by bonding**

Think left to right. $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{MgO}$ are ionic and basic, while $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is ionic with covalent character and amphoteric.

Basic rule:
$$\text{basic oxide + acid} \rightarrow \text{salt + water}$$

**Test statement 1**

All three of those oxides react with acids. $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{MgO}$ neutralise $\text{HCl}$ as bases, and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ also reacts with $\text{HCl}$ because it is amphoteric.

Example:
$$\text{MgO} + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Test statement 2 about metal chlorides in water**

The metal chlorides here are $\text{NaCl}$, $\text{MgCl}_2$ and $\text{AlCl}_3$. Only $\text{NaCl}$ gives a truly neutral solution.

$\text{AlCl}_3$ hydrolyses strongly to give $\text{H}^+$:
$$\text{[Al(H}_2\text{O)}_6\text{]}^{3+} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{[Al(H}_2\text{O)}_5\text{(OH)]}^{2+} + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+$$
So statement 2 is false.

**Test statement 3 about electronegativity**

Electronegativity increases across a period. Of Na, Mg, Al, Si and P, the two most electronegative are Si and P.

Both form simple covalent chlorides, $\text{SiCl}_4$ and $\text{PCl}_3$ / $\text{PCl}_5$, which hydrolyse in water. So statement 3 is true.

**Combine the verdicts**

Statement 1 is true, statement 2 is false, statement 3 is true. That gives 1 and 3 only.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes statement 2. $\text{AlCl}_3$ does not give a neutral solution, it hydrolyses to form an acidic solution with pH around 3. So 1, 2 and 3 cannot all be correct.
options.B: Incorrect because it includes statement 2 but leaves out statement 3. Statement 2 is false due to hydrolysis of $\text{AlCl}_3$ (and slight hydrolysis of $\text{MgCl}_2$), while statement 3 is true.
options.C: Correct. Statement 1 is true as $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, $\text{MgO}$ and amphoteric $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ all react with dilute $\text{HCl}$. Statement 3 is true as Si and P are the most electronegative and form covalent $\text{SiCl}_4$ and phosphorus chlorides. Statement 2 is false.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes the false statement 2 and misses the true statement 1. The ionic oxides $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, $\text{MgO}$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ do all react with dilute hydrochloric acid.
